title: Regional Access Gateway: intake form + prioritization matrix for residency & failover requests
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Purpose: define a single 'Regional Access Gateway' intake artifact and decision matrix teams can use to triage customer requests for new region availability, data residency guarantees, and failover routing. This ticket delivers: (1) a lightweight intake form for Solutions + Sales to capture legal, technical, and commercial constraints; (2) a scored prioritization matrix that balances customer risk/exposure, revenue potential, implementation cost, and capacity lead time; (3) an approval checklist that indicates when the request requires Legal/Compliance, Networking, or Dedicated capacity commitments; (4) example triage outcomes and runbook handoffs for engineering and sales. Scope: non-bug, enterprise requests involving new region provisioning, data residency residency guarantees, or SRE-designated failover zones. Out-of-scope: transient routing performance tweaks, ongoing capacity ops, and low-touch self-serve region toggles.
acceptance_criteria: Intake form PDF + editable Google Sheet exists and collects minimum required fields (customer legal residency, data classification, estimated QPS, SLOs, preferred failover zones, contract terms)
Prioritization matrix with weighted scoring for revenue, legal risk, infra cost, and implementation time is documented and tested against 6 historical customer cases
Decision checklist includes explicit triggers to open Legal/Compliance review and to start Dedicated capacity planning (including estimated lead times)
Handoff templates for ENG, SRE, Sales, and Customer Success with required artifacts (design doc link, PRD, capacity estimate, contract clause)
Pilot triage of 3 queued enterprise requests performed using the artifact with notes and a lessons-learned update
notes_and_tradeoffs: Trade-offs considered: (a) strict residency guarantees increase time-to-ship and cost — we propose a tiered offer (soft residency + contractual residency) to trade latency/cost vs legal certainty; (b) automated prioritization reduces human bias but requires accurate revenue signals — we weight 'existing committed ARR' higher to avoid gaming; (c) pre-reserving capacity for high-tier customers reduces lead time but increases idle cost — recommend a small pool for top-tier customers and on-demand/accelerated provision for others.
implementation_outline: Phase 1 (2 weeks): build intake form and scoring spreadsheet; socialization with Sales/Solutions; perform 3 retrospective scorings. Phase 2 (3 weeks): convert scoring to a one-page decision matrix, add an automated summary template for Legal and ENG triggers, integrate with Linear triage workflow (create ENG ticket when score >= threshold). Phase 3 (4 weeks): implement capacity lead-time table with ENG input and publish pilot SLA language examples for Commercial. Full rollout gated on Legal approval and a pilot run with 3 customers.
